{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent primary endpoint definition in synopsis",
      "quote": "PFS - defined as time from randomization until disease progression or death from any cause, whichever occurs first for all subjects.",
      "page": 10,
      "section": "1.1 Synopsis",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The primary endpoint definition in the synopsis does not mention censoring at start of new anti-cancer therapy, but the estimand description states 'PFS is censored at the date of last evaluable assessment before or on start of new anti-cancer therapy.' This inconsistency could lead to ambiguity in analysis.",
      "fix": "Align the primary endpoint definition with the estimand by adding the censoring rule for new anti-cancer therapy."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing definition of 'treatment-emergent' adverse events",
      "quote": "Subject incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events, treatment-related adverse events, changes in vital signs, and clinical laboratory tests.",
      "page": 10,
      "section": "1.1 Synopsis",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The term 'treatment-emergent' is used but not defined in the synopsis or in the provided text. Without a clear definition, it is unclear whether AEs occurring after treatment discontinuation are included.",
      "fix": "Add a definition of treatment-emergent adverse events (e.g., AEs with onset or worsening after first dose of study drug)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent crossover trigger description",
      "quote": "Once subjects on the docetaxel arm are determined to have radiological progression according to RECIST v1.1 by the investigator and progressive disease undergoes independent central confirmation, they will be given the opportunity to crossover and receive AMG 510.",
      "page": 10,
      "section": "1.1 Synopsis",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The synopsis states crossover is offered after independent central confirmation of progression, but later in the same paragraph it says 'Alternatively, should an early efficacy of the study be noted by the DMC, crossover will be considered for all subjects who randomized into the docetaxel arm.' This creates two different crossover pathways that are not clearly reconciled.",
      "fix": "Clarify the conditions under which each crossover pathway applies and whether DMC-triggered crossover overrides the standard progression-based crossover."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing details on treatment beyond progression",
      "quote": "See Section 8.1.6 and Section 8.1.7 for AMG 510 and docetaxel treatment beyond radiologic progression.",
      "page": 10,
      "section": "1.1 Synopsis",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The synopsis references sections 8.1.6 and 8.1.7 for treatment beyond progression, but these sections are not provided in the text. Without this information, the criteria for continuing treatment after progression are unclear.",
      "fix": "Include the referenced sections or summarize the criteria for treatment beyond progression in the synopsis."
    },
    {
      "title": "Unclear timing of tumor assessments after progression",
      "quote": "Subjects that undergo treatment beyond progression or crossover, from docetaxel to AMG 510, will continue to receive scans after confirmation of first PD.",
      "page": 10,
      "section": "1.1 Synopsis",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The frequency and duration of scans after progression are not specified. The text only says 'continue to receive scans' without detailing the schedule, which could lead to variability in data collection.",
      "fix": "Specify the imaging schedule after progression (e.g., every 9 weeks) and the endpoint for stopping scans."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent definition of 'stable disease' in DCR",
      "quote": "Disease control rate - defined as rate of confirmed objective response (CR or PR) + stable disease per RECIST v1.1 of at least 6 weeks measured",
      "page": 10,
      "section": "1.1 Synopsis",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The phrase 'of at least 6 weeks measured' is grammatically incomplete and ambiguous. It is unclear whether stable disease must be maintained for at least 6 weeks from randomization or from the first assessment.",
      "fix": "Clarify the minimum duration for stable disease (e.g., 'stable disease for at least 6 weeks from randomization')."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing definition of 'major metabolites' in PK objective",
      "quote": "To characterize the pharmacokinetics (PK) of AMG 510 and its major metabolites",
      "page": 10,
      "section": "1.1 Synopsis",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The term 'major metabolites' is not defined. It is unclear which metabolites are considered major and whether they will be quantified in plasma or urine.",
      "fix": "Define 'major metabolites' (e.g., M1 and M2) and specify the matrix for PK analysis."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent use of 'BICR' vs 'independent central confirmation'",
      "quote": "Tumor assessment and response will be confirmed by BICR who will evaluate disease progressions and responses without the knowledge of randomization assignments",
      "page": 10,
      "section": "1.1 Synopsis",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The text uses both 'BICR' and 'independent central confirmation' (COP) without clarifying whether they are the same or different processes. This could cause confusion in operational implementation.",
      "fix": "Define BICR and COP explicitly and state whether they are the same or separate review processes."
    }
  ]
}
